id: # What is corrected of a study, and why (corrections/). `fix`: source (the study's statistics are taken again from
# where `value` says, and formatted as the release formats: an accession of the GWAS Catalog or a URL, then, after
# semicolons, what its file needs: file=, its name in the study's folder if there are several; n=, the N of every SNP
# in place of the file's; a1=, a2=, snp=, chr=, pos=, z=, beta=, se=, or=, the column that plays each role where its
# name does not say so; a study's source comes before its other fixes), flip (Z was signed for A2: its sign is turned), clean
# (rows listed twice, or with a Z that is not a number, are dropped), n (the file's N is not the count of its
# individuals, but an effective N, or a count with samples that its statistics do not hold: each SNP's N is scaled so
# that the largest becomes `value`, the cases and controls of the analysis, as the release counts N for its other
# case-control studies), alleles (the file has one pair of letters at every SNP, and its Z is for the allele that
# `value` says, "second" by the alphabet: each SNP gets its own alleles from the HapMap3 list, that allele first),
# relabel (the file is sound; `value` is the trait it holds). The corrected copies are written
# outside this repository, each with a record of its source, its checksums and what changed.

the file's N, 115,803, is the paper's discovery and replication samples together (47,429 cases and 68,374 controls), but its statistics are of the discovery samples alone: 14,802 cases and 26,703 controls (GWAS Catalog GCST009597). The paper (PMID 31604244) says that only the discovery set had genome-wide coverage, and that the replication typed the 4,842 SNPs chosen in it; the file has 99% of the HapMap3 SNPs. Its share of SNPs with p < 0.05, 7.30%, is about that of the paper's discovery meta-analysis (7.28% of its 8,278,136 SNPs, the MHC among them), and it has 60 regions with a genome-wide significant SNP outside the MHC, where the paper has 82 such effects in the discovery analysis and 200, in 156 regions, with the replication. At the 89 published lead SNPs that the file has, its |Z| is below the published at 87, and 0.60 of it at the 31 strongest, which is the discovery samples' share (0.58 to 0.60); at weaker ones it is more, as it is where SNPs were chosen for their discovery statistics
